builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
summary: The technique replaces unconditional full re-rendering and blocking build-check-render pipelines in code-to-video agent workflows with a training-free execution layer that caches frames by drawing commands and runs checks before rendering at idle priority. It costs additional CPU for speculative rendering that may be discarded when checks fail, plus the complexity of integrating an execution layer behind existing agent commands. It can fail when frame keys miss due to genuinely new content, when recent build history mispredicts check outcomes and wastes render compute, and in domains where the agent's edits rarely produce reusable frames.
rationale: This targets a narrow production setting (code-generated video agents such as Manim workflows) that most AI/ML engineers on constrained infrastructure do not operate, though it is worth adopting if that is the reader's actual workload since it is training-free and framework-agnostic.
technique: Exact frame reuse and blocking-aware build scheduling

claims.statement: The technique replaces unconditional full re-rendering and blocking build-check-render pipelines in code-to-video agent workflows with a training-free execution layer that caches frames by drawing commands and runs checks before rendering at idle priority. It costs additional CPU for speculative rendering that may be discarded when checks fail, plus the complexity of integrating an execution layer behind existing agent commands. It can fail when frame keys miss due to genuinely new content, when recent build history mispredicts check outcomes and wastes render compute, and in domains where the agent's edits rarely produce reusable frames.

CodeReel reduces agent wait by 36.3% against a warm rebuild pipeline and 57.9% against a sequential pipeline; with real agents the median wait per build is 0.62x Rebuild's in Claude Code (a 1.61x speedup) and 0.67x in Codex CLI.
